page: Microsoft Azure E4a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EAv4 server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance offers 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz and features dedicated allocation, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, alongside 102 GB of local storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate a profile suited for memory-bound workloads rather than raw computational speed. The instance registers poor single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak read-only speeds of 198.58 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 27.34 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside poor write performance at 12.95 GB/sec. However, single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression achieve average tier performance. Geekbench scores align with this, showing average single-core capabilities but weak multi-core execution.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4a_v4 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its virtual CPU count, making it a viable option for workloads requiring larger memory footprints without demanding high-performance compute resources. Given its hardware profile, this server is best suited for memory-intensive applications with moderate CPU requirements, such as caching layers, small database operations, and basic web serving.

Powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor running at 3.35 GHz, this x86_64 architecture instance includes 102 GB of local storage and runs on Microsoft Hyper-V. While its CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally fall into the weak to poor categories, it maintains average performance in single-threaded compression tasks. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core makes it a cost-efficient choice for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy multi-core processing, such as caching systems, lightweight database operations, and general-purpose memory-bound applications.
